title: Eliminate tungsten: molybdenum buried wordlines and contacts from U.S. ore
idea: Replace W buried wordlines, bitline contacts and periphery plugs with fluorine-free ALD/CVD molybdenum (MoO2Cl2 precursor) sourced from Colorado/Arizona primary and by-product Mo. Mo's shorter electron mean free path gives lower line resistance than W below ~15 nm, so the buried wordline can be recessed shallower, which also reduces GIDL.
why: Removes China's ~80% tungsten chokepoint and WF6 handling from one of DRAM's four core metals; ~10-20% lower wordline RC at 12 nm-class pitch; near-zero supply risk on that input.

title: Eliminate helium backside cooling: closed-loop hydrogen chuck gas
idea: Etch and implant chucks flow He at 5-20 Torr behind the wafer; swap it for H2 (thermal conductivity 0.18 vs 0.15 W/m-K), confined by a sealed ceramic land, recaptured through a Pd-membrane purifier and recirculated, with chamber H2 sensors interlocked well below the lower explosive limit.
why: Backside cooling is a top fab helium use while Qatar's ~30% of supply is offline; cuts fab He draw 50-80% with equal or better wafer temperature control.

title: Eliminate the quartz crucible: cold-crucible skull-melt Czochralski growth
idea: Melt silicon inside a water-cooled, segmented copper crucible heated by induction so a frozen silicon skull is the only surface touching the melt, then pull the crystal from that self-contained melt and add oxygen deliberately by controlled O2/SiO gas doping to keep gettering behaviour.
why: Removes the single-use Spruce Pine high-purity quartz crucible (>80% concentrated) consumed by every 300 mm ingot, and crucible-borne contamination.

title: Eliminate the sacrificial bulk wafer: porous-silicon lift-off with donor reuse
idea: Grow a 10 um device-grade epi layer on a double-porous-Si release layer, bond it to a carrier wafer cast from low-grade solar silicon, split at the porous layer with a water jet, run the DRAM flow on the transferred layer, and re-polish the CZ donor for 30-50 reuses.
why: DRAM uses only the top ~5 um of a 775 um prime wafer; cuts prime polysilicon and crucible quartz per bit ~20x and lowers wafer cost.

title: Eliminate hafnium, zirconium and ruthenium: rutile TiO2 templated on SnO2 electrodes
idea: Use conductive rutile SnO2 (oxygen-vacancy or F-doped) as the storage-node electrode; its rutile lattice templates ALD TiO2 from TiCl4 and water into the rutile phase at <=300 C, giving k~80-100, with a 0.5 nm Al2O3 interlayer to curb leakage.
why: Hits fact 1's k~70 target without Ru templates (~90% South Africa) or Hf/Zr precursors; ~1.5x Cs at the same aspect ratio, or capacitor AR cut from ~70:1 to ~45:1.

title: Eliminate plasma etch and PFAS gases: catalyst-drilled capacitor holes
idea: Define a silver nanodot catalyst array by block-copolymer self-assembly on a thick sacrificial silicon mold, then immerse in HF/H2O2 so each dot sinks vertically (metal-assisted chemical etching), drilling 15-20 nm holes beyond 100:1; build electrodes in the holes, strip the mold, and recover the silver from the bath.
why: The 60-75:1 capacitor etch burns C4F6/C4F8 (PFAS, high-GWP) in the costliest etchers; room-temperature wet drilling reaches the AR~115 that fact 1 asks for with a fraction of the capital.

title: Eliminate lithography for the cell layer: self-ordered anodic alumina template
idea: Deposit aluminium over the array and anodize it in oxalic or sulfuric acid; hexagonal pores self-order at 25-60 nm pitch with aspect ratios above 1000:1. One coarse imprint of pit seeds pins pore registry to the periphery, the pores host capacitors or vertical channels, and the alumina stays as the dielectric.
why: Removes EUV/multipatterning and high-AR plasma etch for the cell layer, using abundant Al and dilute acid; makes AR>115 capacitors trivial (fact 1).

title: Eliminate indium and gallium: zinc-tin-silicon oxide channels for gain cells
idea: Replace IGZO with amorphous Zn-Sn-Si-O deposited by ALD or sputtering: Si binds oxygen and suppresses vacancies for a very low off-current, while Sn 5s orbitals carry ~15-20 cm2/Vs mobility, all from widely mined elements.
why: China holds ~98% of primary gallium under export controls and indium is a concentrated zinc by-product; this de-risks every oxide-semiconductor DRAM path at no loss in leakage.

title: Eliminate ceria CMP: flowable oxide plus atomic-layer etch-back planarization
idea: Replace ceria-slurry oxide CMP steps with spin-on polysilazane fill cured to SiO2, then planarize by quasi-atomic-layer etch-back that stops on a SiN etch-stop detected optically, so no slurry or pad is used.
why: Ceria abrasive is a rare-earth product dominated by China, and CMP is a top ultrapure-water and waste consumer; removes ~5-10 CMP steps per DRAM flow.

title: Eliminate ultrapure-water rinses: supercritical CO2 cleans that stop pillar collapse
idea: Replace wet clean, rinse and IPA dry after capacitor-mold strip and post-etch steps with supercritical CO2 plus small co-solvent doses, recompressing and reusing >95% of the CO2.
why: Zero surface tension ends capillary collapse of 60-75:1 pillars, allowing AR~100+ capacitors (fact 1), and removes a large share of UPW per wafer.

title: Eliminate neon excimer gas: all-solid-state 193 nm lithography laser
idea: Generate 193 nm light from high-power Yb fiber lasers via frequency conversion and sum-frequency mixing in CLBO crystals, replacing ArF excimer chambers that consume Ne/Ar/F2 gas fills.
why: Removes the neon chokepoint (historically ~50% Ukraine/Russia) and F2 handling for the dozens of DUV immersion layers DRAM still uses; less tool downtime.

title: Eliminate EUV from periodic array layers: one-master nanoimprint templates
idea: Wordline, bitline, landing-pad and storage-node layers are perfectly periodic, so write one e-beam master per layer, replicate imprint templates from it, and pattern by jet-and-flash nanoimprint, keeping DUV only for the aperiodic periphery.
why: Removes 5-7 EUV exposures (fact 4) from a single-supplier tool drawing ~1 MW each; NIL tools cost and consume roughly a tenth as much.

title: Eliminate the wafer fab: oxide gain-cell memory on idle display-glass lines
idea: Build 2T0C oxide-TFT gain-cell arrays on Gen-8.5 glass (~5.5 m2, ~75x a 300 mm wafer) in under-used LCD fabs with 1-1.5 um lithography, then dice tiles for a high-capacity, slower CXL memory tier.
why: Repurposes depreciated capacity with no crucible quartz, no EUV and a <400 C process; ~1/50 the processing cost per m2, offsetting much lower areal density.

title: Eliminate the package: wafer-scale DRAM shipped as unsawn memory wafers
idea: Design arrays with spare-tile routing so the whole 300 mm wafer acts as one memory device, then bond it face-to-face to a logic wafer or to a cold plate with edge connectors, skipping dicing, ABF substrates, solder balls, mold compound and per-die handler test.
why: Eliminates ABF build-up film (single supplier), Sn-Ag solder and gold; ~10-20% off cost per bit from back-end and massive native bandwidth.

title: Eliminate new silicon: harvest and re-certify DRAM from retired servers
idea: Run a reverse-logistics business that pulls DDR4/DDR5 modules from decommissioned hyperscale servers, retention-bins them hot, and redeploys them behind CXL memory expanders with stronger ECC as a second memory tier.
why: Each reused GB avoids new wafer starts, energy and water; could add several percent of global supply within months during the shortage.

title: Eliminate vacuum pumps: atmospheric spatial ALD for capacitor dielectrics
idea: A gas-bearing spatial ALD head separates precursor zones with N2 curtains at atmospheric pressure while the wafer moves beneath it; pulsed-pressure dwell cycles push precursor down high-AR holes.
why: Drops dry pumps (a major share of deposition-tool energy), raises throughput 5-10x and cuts precursor waste; conformality at 70:1 is the open question.

title: Eliminate the ballroom cleanroom: sealed-pod mini-environment fab
idea: Wafers never meet room air: every tool docks sealed nitrogen pods and the building is held only at ISO 8, so HVAC is sized for people, not particles, enabling small modular U.S. memory fabs.
why: Cleanroom HVAC is ~30-50% of fab electricity and a large share of shell capital; cuts both and shortens build time.

title: Eliminate quartz furnace tubes: flash-lamp and microwave anneals
idea: Replace batch diffusion and anneal furnaces (high-purity quartz tubes and boats) with millisecond flash-lamp and volumetric microwave anneals in single-wafer chambers for dopant activation, dielectric crystallization and passivation.
why: Removes recurring Spruce Pine quartzware demand and long furnace thermal cycles; less dopant diffusion also helps the leakage tail (fact 3).

title: Eliminate NF3 cleans: closed fluorine loop with on-site electrolytic F2
idea: Scrub HF from fab exhaust and wet benches, electrolyze it as KF-2HF on site to regenerate F2 for chamber cleaning, and retire purchased NF3 (GWP ~17,000).
why: Cuts dependence on fluorspar (China-dominated) and on concentrated NF3 makers, and removes a potent greenhouse emission.

title: Eliminate ingots and wire saws: kerfless seeded direct-solidified wafers
idea: Freeze 300 mm wafers directly from a silicon melt onto a cooled, seeded template that imposes single-crystal orientation, then high-temperature anneal to drive out dislocations; there is no ingot, no wire saw and no kerf.
why: Kerf wastes ~40% of polysilicon and ingot pulling is energy- and crucible-intensive; halves silicon and energy per wafer if defect density reaches DRAM grade.

title: Eliminate DRAM-only fabs: BEOL MIM 1T1C memory in U.S. logic foundries
idea: Build standalone 1T1C memory chiplets using stacked MIM capacitors in the back-end of existing 22-28 nm U.S. logic processes, as Intel's eDRAM did, at lower density but zero new tooling.
why: Raises U.S. memory output from ~1-2% share using already-built fabs and no EUV; tens of PB per year with no new capex.

title: Eliminate binary storage: three bits per gain cell
idea: Store 8 charge levels on a gain cell's storage node, whose read current maps monotonically to node voltage; read with a column-shared 3-bit SAR ADC and write with a precision DAC plus write-verify.
why: Silicon, water, energy and quartz per bit fall ~2-3x for the same wafer starts.

title: Eliminate photoresist and PFAS: stamped-inhibitor area-selective deposition
idea: Microcontact-stamp a self-assembled inhibitor monolayer pattern from a reusable master onto the wafer; ALD then grows only on unstamped regions, forming hardmask lines directly with no resist, photoacid generator, developer or immersion topcoat.
why: PFAS photoacid generators and topcoats face EU restriction; removes coat/develop tracks and fluorinated chemistry from patterning.

title: Eliminate dissipative bitline charging: stepwise adiabatic charge from idle-bitline tanks
idea: Charge the active bitlines in 8-16 small voltage steps, using idle neighbouring bitline groups as charge reservoirs (stepwise adiabatic charging), and return the charge in reverse steps at precharge so resistive CV2 loss drops by the step count.
why: Bitline sense/restore is the largest slice of activation energy; 8-16 steps cut it ~8-12x using the existing array as the tank, with no inductors or added capacitor material.

title: Eliminate the 8-kilobit page: activate only 512-bit wordline slivers
idea: Split each master wordline into 16 locally gated segments with per-segment sub-wordline drivers so an activate charges only the 512 bitlines that hold the requested burst.
why: Attacks the 128x overfetch (fact 8): ~5.9 pJ per useful bit falls to ~0.4 pJ, >10x per random access, and fewer aggressor rows for row hammer.

title: Eliminate retention requirements: refresh-free banks for short-lived AI tensors
idea: The compiler tags tensors that live <1 ms (activations, pipeline gradients, short-request KV) into ephemeral banks built with ~1 fF low-aspect capacitors on 4x shorter bitlines at 0.6 V, never refreshed; the controller tracks age and copies out anything nearing its retention limit.
why: Removes the high-AR capacitor (PFAS etch, Zr) and refresh for those banks; ~5x lower bitline C times ~2.8x lower V2 gives >10x lower energy per access.

title: Eliminate the memory package: oxide memory built in the logic die's BEOL
idea: Deposit 4-8 tiers of indium/gallium-free oxide 2T0C cells in the upper metal stack of the accelerator die itself at <=400 C, wired by vias a few microns from the compute that uses them.
why: Removes the PHY, TSVs, interposer, separate wafer and package; access energy falls from 3-4 pJ/bit (HBM) to ~0.1-0.3 pJ/bit.

title: Eliminate helium and leakage: liquid-nitrogen-cooled DRAM at 0.4 V
idea: Immerse DRAM stacks in LN2 made on site from air (no helium), retarget access-transistor thresholds for 77 K, and run the array at 0.4-0.5 V, where copper resistance is ~6x lower and the leakage tail vanishes so refresh is dropped.
why: ~6x from V2, refresh removed and smaller drivers give ~10x at the memory; the 77 K plant overhead only pays off when shared with cryo-cooled logic pods.

title: Eliminate TSVs and solder: inductive-coupling links between thinned dies
idea: Stack ~20 um thinned DRAM dies with vertically aligned on-chip spiral coils, passing data by near-field inductive coupling and delivering power through a few large vias or edge rails.
why: Removes most copper TSVs, Sn-Ag microbumps and keep-out zones behind HBM's ~3x area tax (fact 6); ~0.1 pJ/bit versus 3-4 pJ/bit.

title: Eliminate charge pumps: monolayer MoS2 access transistors driven from 1 V
idea: Replace the buried silicon access device with a gate-all-around monolayer MoS2 channel (U.S. molybdenum, refinery sulfur) whose ~2 eV gap and 0.7 nm body give near-zero off-current at 0 V, so the wordline swings 0-1 V straight from VDD with no VPP pump or negative-wordline supply.
why: Wordline energy drops (3 V/1 V)^2 times ~2.5x avoided pump loss, ~20x; also removes the leakage tail behind refresh (fact 3) and the pump area.

title: Eliminate storing what can be recomputed: controller rematerialization engine
idea: The memory controller keeps a small recipe table for pages derivable from other data (activations from layer inputs, decompressed tensors, positional tables) and regenerates them in a near-memory MAC array on access instead of fetching them.
why: A 3 nm op costs ~0.1-1 pJ versus ~10-20 pJ per DRAM bit moved, >10x per avoided access, and 20-40% less DRAM capacity has to be bought.

title: Eliminate regulator losses: series-stacked bank domains recycle bitline charge
idea: Stack four bank groups in series across 4x0.5 V rails so charge dumped from one bank's bitlines flows down to power the next domain instead of to ground, with a small switched-capacitor balancer absorbing load mismatch.
why: Charge is reused ~3-4 times and pump/LDO losses (~2.5x) vanish, together ~10x lower energy per activation.

title: Eliminate long bitlines: 16-cell micro-bitlines over a hybrid-bonded sense layer
idea: Fabricate the cell-array wafer and a CMOS sense-amp wafer separately and hybrid-bond them at ~0.5 um pitch so every 16-cell bitline segment lands on its own sense amplifier below.
why: Bitline C drops from ~40-60 fF to ~3 fF, >10x lower activation energy, and Cs can shrink to ~1 fF, removing the 70:1 capacitor (facts 1 and 7).

title: Eliminate stored zeros: zero-line bitmaps keep sparse tensors off DRAM
idea: The controller keeps a 1-bit-per-64-byte zero map in on-die SRAM; all-zero lines and zero-dominant lines (run-length encoded) are never written to or read from the DRAM array.
why: ReLU-sparse activations, pruned weights and optimizer states with 50-90% zero lines see 2-10x fewer accesses, >10x on the sparsest tensors, and freed capacity.

title: Eliminate refresh and capacitors: complementary oxide-TFT static latch cell
idea: Build a cross-coupled latch from n-type Zn-Sn-O and p-type SnO thin-film transistors stacked in the BEOL; wide-gap off-current near 1e-19 A means the static cell draws almost nothing yet never needs refresh, and reads non-destructively at ~100 mV differential swing.
why: Removes the capacitor, the 46 fJ/bit refresh and the restore step; low-swing non-destructive reads are ~10x cheaper, using only abundant elements.

title: Eliminate the clock: asynchronous self-timed DRAM without DLLs or ODT
idea: Replace DDR's DLL, clock tree and on-die termination with a four-phase bundled-data handshake over short in-package links; each bank signals completion, so an idle interface burns nothing.
why: DLL, clocking and termination are a large share of DRAM I/O power even when idle; I/O energy falls from ~5 to <0.5 pJ/bit on short channels.

title: Eliminate transistor leakage: bistable SiC nano-relay memory cells
idea: Each cell is a ~100 nm electrostatically actuated SiC or TiN beam that snaps between two buckled stable states and closes a contact for a zero-leakage read; switching costs aJ of mechanical energy plus wiring.
why: Zero off-current removes refresh and the leakage tail, and the tiny switched charge makes access energy wire-limited, >10x below DRAM; contact endurance is the open risk.

title: Eliminate the half-VDD precharge: single-ended precharge-to-ground sensing
idea: Bitlines rest at 0 V and only cells storing 1 lift their bitline, which a current-mirror sense amp compares against a reference cell; restore drives only the 1s, with no VBLP generator or equalization, and data are bit-plane encoded to be mostly zeros.
why: Bitline energy scales with the count of 1 bits; bit-plane encoded AI data at ~90% zeros gives up to ~10x lower array energy per access.

title: Eliminate low-order bits until needed: MSB-first bit-plane fetch
idea: Store tensors bit-plane transposed across sub-rows so the controller fetches the top 2-4 bit planes first; attention screening or early-exit logic requests the lower planes only for the ~5-10% of values that matter.
why: KV-cache attention moves ~8-12x fewer bits for the same answer, cutting energy per useful value and effective capacity demand.

title: Eliminate the 1 V array: 0.25 V storage with auto-zeroed sense amps
idea: Store and sense at 0.25 V from an efficient buck rail and run all long data wires at 50-100 mV, using offset-cancelling sense amps that sample their own offset onto a capacitor before each activate.
why: Bitline and data-line CV2 drop ~16x; the 4x lower field across the capacitor lets thin Al2O3/TiO2 stacks replace Hf/Zr high-k.

title: Eliminate the data highway: dot-product units in each mat's sense-amp stripe
idea: Put an 8-bit column-serial MAC tree in every mat's sense-amp stripe so weights stay in the row buffer, activations are broadcast in, and only partial sums leave the bank.
why: Data never crosses the die or the I/O: ~4 pJ/bit effective drops to ~0.3 pJ/bit, and fewer HBM stacks (TSV copper, 3x area) are needed for the same throughput.

title: Eliminate ESD and I/O drivers: protection-free hybrid-bonded memory pins
idea: When DRAM is wafer-bonded to logic and never handled as a bare die, delete the ESD diodes, thick-oxide drivers and termination on every data pin and drive ~50 fF bond pads at 0.4 V from core devices.
why: ESD and pad capacitance dominate I/O energy; pin energy falls from pJ to ~10-50 fJ per bit (>10x), and I/O periphery area (fact 7) shrinks.

title: Eliminate the Boltzmann tax: all-silicon bilayer tunnel-FET periphery at 0.3 V
idea: Build decoders, sense control and datapath from electron-hole bilayer tunnel FETs in silicon (no Ge or III-V indium), whose band-to-band switching allows sub-60 mV/decade slopes and a 0.3 V supply.
why: Periphery is ~49% of the die and much of the access energy; 0.3 V versus 1.1 V cuts its CV2 ~13x.

title: Eliminate writability for frozen weights: via-programmed 3D ROM replaces DRAM
idea: Encode a deployed model's weights as present/absent vias in 4-8 stacked metal layers written by maskless e-beam on mature-node wafers, read by low-swing sensing with no refresh or capacitor, with only activations kept in DRAM.
why: Weights are ~50% of inference memory; ROM reads at ~0.05 pJ/bit with zero refresh and frees DRAM supply, using no EUV or high-AR capacitor.

title: Eliminate energy-blind memory buying: pJ-per-bit indexed offtake contracts
idea: A hyperscaler and DOE consortium guarantees 7-year premium offtake for memory measured at <=0.5 pJ per useful bit under a public JEDEC-style energy test, with CHIPS grants for converting U.S. lines to such products.
why: Makes 10x-energy designs bankable; each 10x cut trims data-center power, grid build-out and cooling water.

title: Eliminate silicon interposers: glass-core panel interposers put DRAM 2 mm away
idea: Mount memory dies on glass-core panel interposers (abundant borosilicate, 2 um lines, through-glass vias) within ~2 mm of the processor, driving unterminated low-swing links in place of CoWoS silicon interposers and ABF substrates.
why: Link energy falls to ~0.3-0.5 pJ/bit versus 10-20 for DDR5 (>10x), escaping the silicon-interposer and ABF chokepoints.
